newsitem.title: UK: Weak UK inflation data help robust gilt climb.
newsitem.headline: Weak UK inflation data help robust gilt climb.

text.p: Weaker-than-expected UK producer price inflation figures provided the catalyst for a robust bounce-back in gilt futures on Monday.
Traders said a 3.2 percent slide in producer input prices in November - a barometer of inflation pressures in the pipeline - helped the March gilt future climb 25/32 to stand at 109-22.
But turnover was light, with 31,264 lots traded by 1641 GMT.
"With the volatility we had last week, there was a lot of nervousness out there," said one trader, adding that both domestic and foreign interests were present.
Domestic political turmoil cast a shadow over the market but failed to ruffle feathers too deeply.
Searing divisions within the ruling Conservative party over Europe deepened when Prime Minister John Major lost his one week parliamentary majority on Friday.

Teresa Gorman, a noted Conservative Eurosceptic, added fuel to the fire on Monday, announcing she would table a motion in parliament next month demanding a referendum on Britain's European Union membership.
But analysts said the markets had weathered political uncertainty for so long that they were used to it.

"It (politics) won't be supportive but it also won't be much of a negative influence," said Kevin Adams, gilts analyst at BZW. Wednesday's meeting between Chancellor Kenneth Clarke and Bank of England Eddie Georgeis widely expected to not sanction any rate rise -- a view only encouraged by the political wrangling.
"The government's in enough hot water over Europe at the moment and the governor's comments last week were a lot more dovish than expected," said the trader.

The March short sterling contract closed at 93.47, versus a Friday close of 93.40, indicating base lending rates of around 6.5 percent by the end of the first quarter against 6.0 percent currently. By December 1997 rates are seen even higher by the market at 7.25 percent.
